        Welcome to the Week 8 grades!This might go down as the most bizarre Sunday in NFL history: We saw one team win a game without completing a single pass, we saw a final score that's never happened before and we saw the Ravens lose two quarterbacks to injury before the first half was even over. Here's a closer look at some of the strange things that happened: 
Baker Mayfield went 0-for-3 passing in the Buccaneers' 16-0 win over the Falcons. That stat line makes the Bucs the first team since 1974 to have zero completions in a win. The Falcons gave up 324 rushing yards to the Bucs, which is the most they've ever surrendered in a game in franchise history. The Ravens became the first team since 2017 to have three different quarterbacks throw a pass in the first half of a game. They lost Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury on the first offensive play and then they ended up losing Tyler Huntley to a toe injury in the second quarter. That left undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as the only healthy QB on the roster. The Bengals beat the Titans 43-36, giving us a scorigami (that means it was the first time in NFL history that final score has ever happened). The Cowboys blew a two-touchdown lead in the fourth quarter, which had never happened before. The Cowboys were 202-0-1 at home when leading by 14 points or more in the fourth quarter before blowing a 24-10 lead and losing to the Cardinals on Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs ran through the Vikings with 153 yards on the ground, making him the first player since 2011 to rush for at least 150 yards against a team that went into a game with a record of 6-0 or better. Speaking of Gibbs, let's get to this week's grades, starting with Detroit's big win. Lions (5-2) 19-15 over Vikings (6-1)Commanders (2-4-1) 27-10 over Eagles (2-6)Broncos (6-2) 28-24 Chiefs (5-2)Rams (4-4) 24-9 over Chargers (0-7)Patriots (5-3) 24-19 over Miami (1-6)Bills (6-1) 36-10 over Ravens (4-4)Steelers (6-2) 27-6 over Browns (5-3)Buccaneers (3-5) 16-0 over Falcons (3-5)Jaguars (5-2) 42-7 over Colts (2-6)Raiders (4-4) 38-33 over Jets (2-6)Bengals (5-2) 43-36 over Titans (1-7)Cardinals (3-5) 33-30 in OT over Cowboys (3-5)Packers (5-3) 27-19 over Panthers (3-4)

title: Five things we learned as Broncos stun Chiefs, seize first place in AFC West - CBS Sports
description: Denver's quarterback delivered another remarkable finish, while a vastly improved defense and two emerging runnin
body:
Denver's quarterback delivered another remarkable finish, while a vastly improved defense and two emerging running backs helped the Broncos take control of the AFC West
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Broncos got one of the best wins by any team this season, coming back from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Chiefs 28-24. Denver got massive, heroic efforts from its offense and its defense, especially in the fourth quarter.Sean Payton and the Broncos moved to the top of the AFC West at 6-2 and erased the head-to-head advantage the Chiefs had entering the game. The Broncos have won four straight games, surviving a brutal opening stretch; they have already faced the Chiefs (twice), the Jaguars, the Rams, the 49ers and the Seahawks. A winning record would have been a success, but 6-2 is a resounding one.It's not just a big result for the division and potential playoff implications, but for what is says about both teams. Games like these -- postseason-caliber matchups -- teach us a lot about where both clubs are and where they could be headed. These are the five lessons we learned.1. Bo Nix's fourth-quarter magic is inexplicable ... and incredibleOne didn't need to watch the first three quarters to comprehend how Bo Nix was playing. The boos on the broadcast told the story. Such is life for a quarterback: goat in the eyes of fans one minute, GOAT the next.
Entering the fourth quarter, Nix was 15-for-26 for 153 yards. Just seven of his 26 attempts had gone for first downs, including just one of eight on third down. It was ugly, and it looked like what Nix had put on display much of the year: very conservative, with little downfield. The boo birds were especially prominent when consecutive drives ended with punts after Nix completed short of the sticks on third down.And then the fourth quarter came. Nix went 5-for-6 for 84 yards. Was it anything magical? No. But Nix took advantage of a pair of coverage busts in crucial moments. First, this touchdown to Nate Adkins:
Then this quick pass to Jonah Coleman:
Since entering the NFL in 2024, Nix has ...15 game-winning drives, most ever in a quarterback's first three seasons12 fourth-quarter comebacks, tied with Derek Carr for most ever in a quarterback's first three seasonsThe Broncos have averaged 8.1 points per fourth quarter under Nix, the highest rate for any starting quarterback since at least 1950.
CBS' broadcast team of Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt explained that when they met with Nix, he couldn't explain his late-game exploits, but it's certainly better to start slow and finish strong than to start strong and finish slow. That much is true.2. The Broncos' run defense has improved significantlyOf course, Nix owes the fact that he even has a chance in the games he starts slow to his defense being excellent. And it very much was Sunday. The last-second goal-line stand is what will get the most plaudits, but Denver's stout defense throughout the game was crucial.That starts with stopping the run. In Week 1, Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards in a 31-10 Chiefs win. There were missed tackles all over the place -- 24 in total -- and just way too many wide-open holes. Walker had 7.8 yards per carry after contact in Week 1. In Week 8? There were still 16 missed tackles, but Walker had just 2.1 yards per carry after contact. He finished with just 69 yards total.
This has been a season-long improvement for Denver.Broncos run defenseWeeks 1-4Weeks 5-8Yards per rush4.84.2Explosive runs118Yards after contact per rush4.13.13. Andy Reid's late-game management remains suspectFor an offensive-minded head coach with one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time, Andy Reid has had some extremely conservative moments as a coach. Sunday, he had another one. Up three with under three minutes left, Mahomes took a bad, bad sack. It wasn't a great play call, but we can't blame Reid for Mahomes taking a rare awful sack.We can blame Reid for kicking on fourth and 8 from the Denver 36-yard line. Harrison Butker missed (very) wide right. He is now 2 for 7 from 50+ yards this year.The execution of the play obviously wasn't what Reid had hoped for, but his thought process there is extremely poor. As I wrote in our weekly overreactions and reality checks:Up three, a field goal helps, but not that much. In fact, if it had gone in, it would have given the Broncos an extra down on their ensuing drive, since they would have needed a touchdown. Going up six is not a good idea in this scenario.Thus, this should have been four-down territory. Could Reid have tried a run on third down? Again, we can't blame him for Mahomes taking a bad sack, but we can blame him for a poor approach.Butker has proved to be unreliable, over and over, this season. This isn't prime Butker. And making matters worse, this was a kick in the rain. When he missed, the Broncos were down just three and had great field position.Mahomes is actually better at converting fourth-and-8 to fourth-and-12 in his career (3 for 6 -- 50%) than Butker is at kicking from 50+ this year. So yes, even though fourth-and-8 looks bad, it might not have been. And Mahomes had been rolling all game. Speaking of ...4. Patrick Mahomes got the passing game back on track, but he needs helpThe Chiefs' collapse will overshadow an otherwise outstanding game from Mahomes. He was 30 for 41 for 321 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions. He took just two sacks against a fearsome pass rush and made several terrific plays while under pressure. His 0.16 EPA per dropback was his best mark since Week 3 and, considering the opponent, it might have been his best game of the year.On third downs, Mahomes was 6 for 10 for 113 yards and a touchdown. Four of his six completions went for first downs, including conversions of third-and-10 and third-and-12.But the Chiefs must upgrade their receiving corps. The Chiefs' leading receiver was running back Emmett Johnson (more on him in a bit) with five catches for 128 yards. Tight end Travis Kelce had five catches for 67 yards. Wide receiver Rashee Rice had seven catches but for just 53 yards, and he is very much a quick-pass and YAC guy.Ever since Tyquan Thornton's injury, Kansas City's deep passing game has evaporated. He has not had a single completion on a throw 20+ yards downfield in any of the past three games, since Thornton's injury. That's tied for the longest streak of his career. (He had seven in the three weeks before that, for comparison's sake.)Whether it's a big name (George Pickens, perhaps?) or a smaller one, Kansas City must add some downfield firepower. Rice doesn't provide it. Xavier Worthy, for all his speed, doesn't provide it. The rest of the guys are young late-round picks or former UDFAs. More downfield pop would help the run game, too.5. Young running backs shineBoth the Broncos and the Chiefs added mid-round running backs in this year's draft. Both were expected to play complementary roles: The Broncos already had J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, and the Chiefs already had Walker.But it's clear that Jonah Coleman and Emmett Johnson deserve more love than the "complementary piece" title suggests. Coleman, in fact, led the Broncos in carries (11), rushing yards (41) and receiving yards (63). He also scored the game-winning touchdown. With Harvey out, he looks like a lead back.
Johnson, meanwhile, also found the end zone. In addition to his 128 receiving yards, he had a 15-yard carry and a 44-yard kick return. He looked like Walker was making would-be tacklers miss on a consistent basis. This was an excellent play design, and look at how Johnson finishes it.
The Chiefs can't run Walker into the ground. Expect Johnson to continue to see significant action.

title: Former Cowboys QB rips Dallas for 'embarrassing' loss to Cardinals: 'They stink' - CBS Sports
description: The loss was bad enough, but the way the Cowboys crumbled did not sit well with the 2020 draft pick
body:
The loss was bad enough, but the way the Cowboys crumbled did not sit well with the 2020 draft pick
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Dallas Cowboys have never won a game against the Arizona Cardinals inside AT&T Stadium. With their Week 8 loss, they fell to 0-5 in such contests. The 33-30 overtime defeat was undoubtedly the most disappointing result of the bunch. In fact, former Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci chalked it up as an "embarrassing" loss.Despite holding a 10-point lead with 3:54 to play in regulation, the Cowboys lost for the third time in the last four weeks. They led by as many as 14 points in the fourth quarter and for the first time this century lost a home game with that kind of late advantage. They had won each of their last 69 such games. It was as disheartening of a showing as any across the NFL."This was absolutely embarrassing today," DiNucci said on CBS Sports HQ. "They stink. I'm lost for words, honestly. They have so much talent on both sides of the ball, and year after year, week after week, all we see is just letdowns from them. I'm not sure what needs to change. … But at some point, the same old, same old in Dallas for the Cowboys, it's not cutting it. Something needs to change. Somebody needs to look themselves in the mirror. I don't know who it is, but that was an embarrassing loss for them."Dallas was fortunate to even have a second chance at winning the game in overtime, because if not for a missed extra point on the Cardinals' final touchdown, they would have almost certainly lost in regulation.
Adding insult to injury, Arizona sparked its comeback with a backup quarterback. Gardner Minshew entered in relief of Jacoby Brissett and instantly elevated the offense with some help from running back Tyler Allgeier. What's more, the Cardinals may be destined to finish the year in last place in the NFC West. That is the caliber of opponent the Cowboys need to defeat in order to accomplish their goal of winning their own division, which remains fully up for grabs."It comes down to effort for the Dallas Cowboys," DiNucci said. "When you turn on the tape week in and week out -- and I honestly hate questioning guys' effort in the NFL because all of us understand what goes on on a day-to-day and week-to-week basis inside those locker rooms and organizations -- but the effort is not there for the Cowboys. You never know what team you're getting week in and week out. You can tell run play from pass play based on what effort guys are giving on offense."The changes that DiNucci called for might not include a coaching change. Team owner Jerry Jones indicated that firing Brian Schottenheimer in the middle of the season is not on the table. If not that, then what? There are only so many ways to spark a meaningful turnaround when a team is seemingly at rock bottom.
DiNucci understands the pressure that comes with wearing the Cowboys star, having spent the 2020 and 2021 seasons as the team's backup quarterback, and he said the star veterans need to step up and change the culture."At some point, something inside that locker room needs to change," DiNucci said. "The leaders, whoever it is: Dak Prescott, Quinnen Williams, CeeDee Lamb. Whoever it is, somebody needs to take control of that locker room and say, 'Guys, whatever we're doing right now is simply not working. We need to scrap this thing. We need to ignore the outside noise.'"I think a lot of the problem in Dallas is there's so much going on outside the game of football there. It's hard for guys to compartmentalize football from what's going on off the field. I can say that. I was there for a couple of years. I saw it firsthand on Mondays and Tuesdays; when I'm working out on off days, they're running tours through the facility, letting people see us work out and meetings and this and that. There's just a lot that comes with being a Dallas Cowboys football player, and I wonder if that at some point starts to take a toll on guys."
There are a few get-right opportunities in the near future for Dallas with the Indianapolis Colts, Tennessee Titans and Philadelphia Eagles representing three of their next four opponents. If a week off is what this team needs, though, that will not come until a Week 14 bye.

title: College football coaching carousel 2026: Tracking all the changes so far - CBS Sports
description: Get the latest on the college football coaching carousel as CBS Sports tracks new hires and fires
body:
Get the latest on the college football coaching carousel as CBS Sports tracks new hires and fires
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a few false starts, the coaching carousel finally started spinning in late October.It's not surprising the silly season is off to a slow start after 2025's record-breaking churn. The FBS hired 32 new head coaches, including 17 in the four power conferences, and hundreds more assistant coaches changed jobs.Ninety-three FBS programs have changed coaches over the last three offseasons. The question is whether we've hit a cooling period as schools wrestle with the challenging economics of the NIL and revenue-sharing era. Maryland kicked off the firing season Oct. 21. More power programs have followed. CBS Sports is tracking every move in the 2026-27 cycle and grading each hire below.Power Four
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Baylor -- OUT: Dave Aranda | IN: TBDDave Aranda won a Big 12 title in 2021 but otherwise led the Bears with middling success over seven seasons. He finished 40-40 and was below .500 in the Big 12 (26-32). Don't be surprised if Baylor seeks an offensive coach, particularly one with strong connections to the Texas high school scene. UTSA's Jeff Traylor, Texas State's GJ Kinne and USC's Lincoln Riley are strong candidates to consider in Waco.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Florida State -- OUT: Mike Norvell | IN: TBDAfter seven whirlwind seasons, which included an undefeated campaign in 2023 while being snubbed from the College Football Playoff, Florida State cut ties with Norvell on Nov. 1 following a loss to Clemson. Is FSU as lucrative a job as it has been in the past? We'll find out as questions surround the financials of the program. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Maryland -- OUT: Mike Locksley | IN: TBDMaryland kicked off the coaching carousel this year. Mike Locksley is out halfway through his eighth season at Maryland, where he was 39-54 overall. The Terps were 4-8 in back-to-back seasons leading to the decisive 2026. A wide variety of candidates will be considered in College Park. Wake Forest's Jake Dickert, a popular name elsewhere, and Memphis' Charles Huff, a Maryland native, immediately come to mind. The Terps have better NIL resources than a year ago, but the job is still difficult in the Big Ten.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    NC State -- OUT: Dave Doeren | IN: TBD
Dave Doeren is out after 14 years in Raleigh, following a disappointing 31-28 loss at Stanford that dropped the Wolfpack to 1-3 in the ACC. Doeren seemed just good enough to win seven to nine games every year, but disappointing losses always railroaded what could have been special seasons. A downtick in success over the last three years made it clear a change was needed. The candidate with the most heat is legendary NC State quarterback Philip Rivers. He's coached high school football for five years in Alabama and interviewed for the Buffalo Bills' job in January. His son, Gunner, is committed to NC State. This job has a wide variety of potential candidates, including Miami offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson, UNLV's Dan Mullen and Memphis' Charles Huff.

title: Why Jerry Jones 'doesn't see' firing Brian Schottenheimer midseason after disaster Cowboys loss to Cardinals - CBS Sports
description: Dallas squandered a 14-point fourth-quarter lead in its overtime loss to Arizona, but Jones says he is not consid
body:
Dallas squandered a 14-point fourth-quarter lead in its overtime loss to Arizona, but Jones says he is not considering an in-season coaching change
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:35 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ARLINGTON, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys (3-5) did the unthinkable in their 33-30 overtime home defeat against the Arizona Cardinals (3-5).Dallas led by 14 points twice, including 24-10 with 14:20 left to play, yet still lost. Sunday marked the first loss in Cowboys history when Dallas led by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter. Previously, the Cowboys were 202-0-1 at home when leading by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter, including the playoffs. Dallas' five games with 30-plus points are tied for the most in the NFL with the Buffalo Bills (6-1), but the Cowboys joined the Houston Texans (2-5) as the only two teams with multiple losses when scoring 30 or more points in 2026. The Cowboys defense has now allowed 20-or-more points in 15 consecutive games, which is the longest active streak in the entire league. What does that mean for Brian Schottenheimer? Jerry Jones faced those questions head-on when speaking immediately after Sunday's grisly loss. "Yeah, we're not going to get into anything. That's not in my mind at this time. But the main thing that's in my mind is we tee it up for those kinds of spots to win it," Jones said when asked about a coaching change. "We really do want those situations to call for it, bring it on. And we got it and didn't get it. ... None of us are getting it done, and that should be my concern. So I'm not pointing at Schotty. I'm not pointing to anybody, but none of us have it done. I haven't been involved in too many games that we should have wanted, and we had the opportunities we had to win this game. So that is a big snapshot that we want to put above our mirror."   
Jones has only made one in-season coaching change in his 38 years owning the Cowboys, and that was when he fired Wade Phillips during the 2010 season. Schottenheimer won't be joining Phillips on that list at this time. "I made a change, and I don't want to mention it because I'm not proud of it," Jones said. "But I made a change with Wade Phillips there in the middle of the season, and I don't see that here."  Dallas is 10-14-1 in the Schottenheimer era and has yet to put together a winning streak in 2026. Jones, however, pointed fingers at everyone and not just his coach. 
"It just really is glaring in a negative way how we could be where we were and end up losing that ball game," Jones said. "We had a great chance right at the end to win the game, and had everybody out there that can win games for us, and of course. didn't get it done. So it was a couple of games within the game really that was also telling, and we just just did not play well enough at all to win that ball game. Not well enough after you had the lead the way we did and had the opportunities we had to win that ball game. So it's an indictment of the whole show."        Despite the lack of consistency under Schottenheimer, firing Schottenheimer during the 2026 isn't on his mind at the moment because he feels the inconsistency this season has to do with the entire organization, not just the head coach.   "Well, I will say that a lot of people let Brian down today," Jones said. "So for whatever criticism we want to have with Brian, we can all get in line. And that was a total team loss to use a cliche. That was a total team effort out there for us. And we have to be better for our fans, have to be better than that when we got our hands on the win and then drop the ball."    
Why Prescott won't blame coachingDallas quarterback Dak Prescott was quick to point fingers at himself and many others in addition to the criticism for Schottenheimer. "It's all of us," he said. "Don't put the blame on one person. Simple as that. I think that's weak. I think that's cowardice. "This game is about all 11 that touch the field and every person that has a part in it coaches and support staff. It's never just one person's fault. Even if I go out there and throw a bunch of interceptions, it's never just truly one  person's fault. And so, don't take the easy and cheap way out. This is about us, and it's about us backing him up and  backing one another up and we'll have to show it."   Schottenheimer himself took accountability for the defeat but also deflected to the positive takeaways from Sunday's overtime loss.
"I'm going to always own my part of this as a head football coach. It starts with me and there's certainly things that I need to do better," Schottenheimer said. "But as a football team in all three phases, I can point out three, four, five, six plays right off the top of my head; I'm not going to, about that. And so, a lot of football left, and again, no different than Philadelphia, where you have to come out of that game and say, okay, hey, we didn't reinvent the game. You got to come out of this game and find the positives. There's going to be positives, the way we played in the first half. Quinnen Williams got some pass rush. So  that's what we'll do." Defensively, Dallas' defense allowed backup quarterback Gardner Minshew to come off the Cardinals' bench to become the first player in the NFL this season with at least three passing touchdowns in the fourth quarter of a game. Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier exploded for 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns with a career-high 147 yards rushing on just 11 carries. He ran for a 63-yard score and also added a 52-yard run down the left sideline. That made him the first player in the entire league in 2026 with multiple 50-yard runs in the same game.

title: Week 8 overreactions: Time for Vikings to bench Kyler Murray? Colts should fire Steichen? - CBS Sports
description: For much of the first seven weeks of the season, the predominant question around the Minnesota Vikings was: "Can they really keep winnin
body:
For much of the first seven weeks of the season, the predominant question around the Minnesota Vikings was: "Can they really keep winning this way?"And the answer was yes, six times over. Sure, Minnesota's 10 touchdowns were the fewest by any 6-0 team in more than 100 years, but wins are wins, and Minnesota was stacking them.This week, that ended. The Lions grounded out an impressive 19-15 win, a crucial result in the cutthroat NFC North. Jahmyr Gibbs had 168 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown, and Jared Goff gutted through a tough day overall to throw the game-winning touchdown to Jameson Williams.There were major, uncomfortable questions during the Vikings' winning streak. Those questions just came to the forefront even more with a loss, and the Vikings must find answers immediately. The most important question revolves around the most important position.
Vikings should bench Kyler MurrayOverreaction or reality: RealityI gave Murray a lot of grace early this year. He was on a new team and in a new system. He suffered a concussion moments into his Vikings debut. It was about as inauspicious a start as possible, and even as he struggled after he returned, I was willing to give him some time to figure it out.That time is over. Murray was dreadful again Sunday: 17-for-29 for 210 yards, one touchdown and one interception, with three sacks taken. He also ran four times for 35 yards, which was a team high (more on that in a bit). His touchdown pass was a miraculous Justin Jefferson catch.
But Murray was so wildly inaccurate that he often didn't even give his teammates chances to make otherworldly catches or routine catches. According to TruMedia, five of Murray's 29 passes (17.2%) were off-target. He missed Jefferson up the seam on what would have been a touchdown. He missed Jefferson on a rollout, firing the ball several feet above his superstar wide receiver. He dirtied a ball when Jefferson was open on a slant, a play that left Jefferson shrugging as if to say, "What happened?"
Then, there are far too many throws that have an extremely low likelihood of being completed anyway. He throws a ton of perimeter passes that are 50/50 balls at best, and usually, they're closer to 10/90 balls because Murray is so inaccurate on those, too.He also rarely finds or takes easy answers. His 3.20 average time to throw is by far the highest of his career, even though he is also having the slowest time to pressure this season. Only three players — Caleb Williams, Malik Willis and Drake Maye — have a longer time to throw, on average. But Murray isn't the playmaker or physical force Williams or Maye are.It's a huge surprise to see Murray play this poorly. Even at his worst in Arizona, he was an average or slightly below average quarterback by most metrics. But this season, he has been so much worse than he's ever been.
Kyler Murray career worsts this seasonPrevious career worstEPA per dropback-0.11-0.01Off-target rate13.0%12.4%Passing success rate39.1%44.3%Pass TD pct3.2%3.7%Pressure rate35.9%34.5%Murray's mobility and pocket management have declined, too. He can still move as a runner, but his sack rate and sack-to-pressure rates are way up.Simply put, it's time for the Vikings to look elsewhere, whether that's in-house (Carson Wentz is the backup) or via a trade. Frustration is bubbling up — Jefferson declined to speak to the media after Sunday's game — and in his postgame press conference, Kevin O'Connell mentioned multiple missed opportunities.
O'Connell can only do so much, though. Murray hasn't been close to good enough for a team with a championship-level defense, and Minnesota simply can't keep the status quo much longer.Colts need to part ways with Jonathan Taylor, Shane SteichenOverreaction or reality: RealityThe Colts played one of the worst excuses you'll see for a football game Sunday, falling to the Jaguars 42-7. Indianapolis' first-half drive chart was as follows:puntpuntpuntfumblepuntpuntinterception (pick six)kneelTrevor Lawrence threw for 210 yards and three touchdowns on 14 attempts, a ridiculous 15 yards per attempt — the highest rate by any quarterback in any game (min. 10 attempts) in the last two seasons. The Jaguars also averaged 5.5 yards per carry, and only one of their 33 carries went for negative yards.The offense was similarly embarrassing.
Yes, the Colts traded away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner this week and fired GM Chris Ballard the week before. Yes, the season has gone off the rails. But the Titans traded Jeffery Simmons this week and took the Bengals to overtime. The Colts, on the other hand, didn't look interested in playing. This wasn't acceptable in any way, shape or form, and it falls on Shane Steichen.Here's Jonathan Taylor:
Speaking of Taylor, the Colts reportedly aren't actively shopping him, but not trading him would be a massive mistake. Indianapolis is facing a multi-year rebuild. They have no competent quarterback and likely no way to find one in the draft due to the Sauce Gardner trade. Taylor is reportedly commanding significant offers. The Vikings would be a great fit, as their running game continues to stink.Indianapolis must move their star running back, and it must move on from Steichen, too. If not, it's a damning mismanagement by Carlie Irsay-Gordon at an absolutely critical junction early in her ownership.Browns will never win a regular-season game in Pittsburgh againOverreaction or reality: RealityJust kidding! But boy, a 27-6 loss was a rough dose of reality for the Browns, who haven't won a regular-season game at the Steelers since 2003.Browns should bench Deshaun WatsonOverreaction or reality: OverreactionSpeaking of a rough dose of reality for the Browns, Watson was once again pretty poor Sunday. Though the passing box score stats look good (27-for-39, 324 yards), he took eight sacks. He has now taken 22 sacks in his last four games, a completely unsustainable number. This has been an issue throughout his time in Cleveland, and after a better start to the year avoiding sacks, he has fallen back significantly. He has had a negative EPA per play in three of his past four games, too.But the Browns don't have a better answer. Shedeur Sanders had major sack problems last year. The offensive line is in rough shape. Watson may be back on his downward trajectory, but Cleveland is still 5-3, and Watson has had some good moments in clutch time. All five of the Browns' wins are by four points or fewer. Plus, there's not a better alternative. If there were, Sanders would be starting.Buccaneers will win the NFC SouthOverreaction or reality: RealityBaker Mayfield did not complete a single pass in the Buccaneers' 16-0 win over the Falcons on Sunday, a game played in an absolutely downpour. Let's take a little history lesson.It's the first time since 1974 a team has won a game without a completion.It's the first time since 1945 a team won a game by double digits without a completion.It's the first time a team has had zero completions and 300+ rushing yards since 1933.Mayfield only attempted three passes. The week before, he only attempted 11 (completing seven) in a 43-13 domination of the Panthers. Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards in that game.The Buccaneers cannot win this way forever, clearly. But they don't have to be that far off. The offensive line has really come together after a rocky start, and Bucky Irving looks absolutely excellent. The bigger factor here is the defense, which held Michael Penix Jr. to 8-for-24 passing for 125 yards and four(!) interceptions.
Penix was absolutely atrocious, but this isn't a one-off occurrence. Tampa Bay absolutely dominated Carolina with a relentless pass rush the week before, and this defense has been stupendous all season:First in EPA per playFirst in turnovers forcedSecond in success rateFifth in yards per playFifth in percentage of plays for 0 or negative yardsIt's not like the bar is that high in the NFC South, and the Buccaneers' defense is the best single unit in the division. If Mayfield can avoid making multiple back-breaking mistakes per game, the Buccaneers will join the 1992 Chargers as the only teams to make the postseason after starting 0-4.Bengals can't win the Super Bowl with this defenseOverreaction or reality: OverreactionThe Bengals needed a six-touchdown day from Joe Burrow to beat the lowly, Jeffery Simmons-less Titans 43-36 in overtime. It's a score and a storyline all too familiar for Cincinnati, which has had defensive issues for years.But even after Sunday's poor performance, Cincinnati's defense is only 16th in EPA per play. Why? Well, the Bengals have the third-highest sack rate in the NFL and the fourth-highest rate of 0 or negative yards gained. They are the league's best fourth-down defense. The defense has forced 11 turnovers, too, a top-10 number.
Listen, it's not necessarily the way you want to live. The Bengals are 25th in yards per play allowed and 30th in explosive play rate allowed. But this passing offense is truly elite. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both had 10+ catches, 140+ yards and a touchdown, and as I wrote last week, the latter is only getting better.Plus, the defense has an absolute game-changer in Dexter Lawrence, who has been the best defensive acquisition of the offseason. He saved the game late in regulation.
An elite offense plus a play-making defense? Again, it's far from perfect, but it might be enough.Andy Reid blew itOverreaction or reality: RealityThe Broncos deserve a ton of credit for rallying from a 24-13 deficit in the fourth quarter to beat the Chiefs 28-24. Bo Nix came up clutch, leading touchdown drives on both of Denver's final two possessions, and the defense had a huge goal-line stand to seal the deal. It was an absolutely crucial win for the Broncos, who erased Kansas City's head-to-head advantage from Week 1.
But this comeback doesn't happen without the help of Andy Reid. His offense's final three drives finished as follows: punt, missed field goal, turnover on downs.The missed field goal and the sequence leading up to it will be the main talking point, but let's go chronologically. Early in the fourth quarter, up by 11, Patrick Mahomes threw a 5-yard pass to Emmett Johnson on third-and-6. Really, though, Johnson gained almost 5 yards. It set up fourth and inches. According to the CBS broadcast, Reid was upset that the officials took so long to figure out the spot — he thought it was going to be fourth-and-a-full 1 yard, or maybe more — which forced him to punt. Had he known the spot earlier, he might have gone for it.This is a bad look. Reid should have gone for this regardless. He had Mahomes, his superstar quarterback, playing at a high level. Though the Chiefs did not run the ball well Sunday, all 22 of their rushes to that point had gained at least 1 yard. This is another spot where the Chiefs' inability to run a quarterback sneak — Mahomes hasn't attempted one since 2019 — loomed large. Teams must have a way to gain 1 yard, or, in this instance, a few inches, reliably.But the even worse decision came with just under three minutes left. Up three and facing a third-and-2 at the Denver 30, Reid called an awkward rollout that was immediately stymied. Mahomes took a 6-yard sack — an uncharacteristic and untimely error — to set up fourth-and-8. Then Reid trotted out Harrison Butker for a 54-yard field goal attempt in the rain. He missed (very) wide right.There are so many issues here:
Up three, a field goal helps, but not that much. In fact, if it had gone in, it would have given the Broncos an extra down on their ensuing drive, since they needed a touchdown. Going up six is not a good idea in this scenario.Thus, this should have been four-down teritory. Could Reid have tried a run here? We can't blame him for Mahomes taking a bad sack, but we can blame him for a poor approach.Butker was 2-for-6 from 50+ yards this year entering that kick. He has proved to be unreliable. It's an awful decision from a process and an execution standpoint from Reid.Then late in the game, the Chiefs couldn't punch it in, and their lack of urgency was befuddling. After Kenneth Walker III got down to the 4-yard line with about a minute left, Walker ran 3 yards on a play with 35 seconds left. Then Kansas City didn't take a timeout until there were 15 seconds left, making run plays risky and eliminating any room for error. Mahomes threw an incompletion on second down, and Walker went nowhere on third-and-goal. That forced Reid to use his final timeout. The false start pushed it back to the 6, and Mahomes got sacked. A little more urgency would have kept the playbook more wide open.

Tyler Allgeier takes over Arizona's backfield after Jeremiyah Love's injury, Adonai Mitchell breaks out for the Jets, and Cam Ward flashes dual-threat upside

        Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season started extra slow and not just in the touchdowns department -- there wasn't a lot of offensive total yards in the first halves of the early slate -- but things changed fast. Several key players broke out and that includes more than a few who could help you get a jump-start on your Week 9 lineups via the waiver wire. Let's take a look at early waiver wire standouts for all Fantasy football league formatsWaiver wire standouts of the weekCam Ward, QB, Titans  It was a coming-out party for Ward and the Titans pass game in an unexpected game script and matchup. This year, the Bengals have stepped up on defense, but Week 8 looked like an old-school Bengals shootout, and Ward racked up his first career 300-plus passing game. He finished with 304 yards passing and two touchdowns. He also expanded on his dual-threat ability by scrambling for 41 rushing yards on seven attempts. The Titans have a bye in Week 9, but Ward is worth monitoring in one-QB leagues and should be rostered in any shallow superflex leagues where he was previously released. Tyler Allgeier, RB, Cardinals It has been a frustrating season for Fantasy football managers who used an early-round draft pick on top-five NFL draft pick Jeremiyah Love. After battling an ankle sprain from the preseason, Love has missed several weeks before returning in Week 8. However, early in Week 8, Love left the game with another ankle injury. In his absence, the Cardinals finally saw Allgeier separate himself from Bam Knight in this backfield. Allgeier racked up 147 rushing yards on 11 carries with a long touchdown. He also made a massive impact in the passing game with 44 yards and a receiving touchdown on five catches. If Love is forced to miss action, Allgeier could emerge as an RB2. While we don't expect him to take over the workhorse role, it seems likely Arizona will lean more heavily on Allgeier than Knight moving forward. Adonai Mitchell, WR, JetsMitchell looked awesome in Week 8 and his touchdown in the red zone featured one of the smoothest releases off the line of scrimmage that we've seen all season long. Mitchell saw constant one-on-one matchups with the defense doing its best to take away Garrett Wilson and he delivered. On nine targets, Mitchell totaled 142 receiving yards, seven receptions and that red zone touchdown. 
Gardner Minshew, QB, CardinalsThe Cardinals made the decision to bench Jacoby Brissett in Week 8, and it was a merit-based decision. Minshew immediately provided a spark for the offense and the Cardinals came back to win one of the most improbable victories of the NFL season. It's difficult to imagine the Cardinals turning back to Brissett based on that result, and if they stick with Minshew, he'll be worth adding in all superflex formats. Emmett Johnson, RB, ChiefsThe best handcuff in Fantasy football proved to be more than that in Week 8. Operating as Kansas City's third-down back, Johnson ripped off a 73-yard receiving score and cracked over 100 receiving yards in Week 8. Unfortunately, it will be difficult to predict his scoring upside, but he is one of the best players to stash on your bench. An injury to starter Ken Walker would put Johnson in the RB2 and borderline RB1 range right away. Standout Fantasy performancesHarold Fannin Jr., TE, Browns Fannin is a machine that cannot be stopped right now. Last week the Browns figured out they can use Fannin as an extension of their run game due to his ridiculous ability to force missed tackles and create yards after contact and he once again operated as the engine of the offense. Fannin saw 12 targets, caught 10 of them and turned that into 154 receiving yards. He is emerging as a top-five play at tight end, specifically in PPR formats. 
Bucky Irving, RB, Buccaneers He's back, baby! Bucky once again looks like his rookie-season self and the Buccaneers are putting more on his plate than ever before. He has emerged as the foundation of the offense. Sure, the game script has played a factor in some very run-heavy approaches of late, but this Buccaneers defense is for real. The game plan could continue as is and that led to 170 rushing yards, a touchdown and a whopping 27 carries in WEek 8.

        Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field after appearing to suffer a serious injury during the team's Week 8 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.Following the 19-15 victory, Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters he had no further information on Jack's status, other than that he was receiving medical care.On the first play of the fourth quarter, Campbell and teammate Eric O'Neill combined to tackle Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. Campbell then went limp. While lying prone, he was seen moving his head up and down and pulling his body forward a couple of inches before trainers reached him. After about 10 minutes, Campbell was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field. 
The Lions announced that Campbell was transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury. It was an emotional scene at Ford Field. The entire Lions team went over to see their teammate off, while the defense gathered for a moment to rally after seeing one of their leaders go down. 
In seven games this season, Campbell recorded 57 tackles, two QB hits and a fumble recovery. Just six months ago, he signed a four-year, $81 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid off-ball linebackers in the NFL. 
Campbell was selected with the No. 18 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Iowa, just six selections after the Lions drafted running back Jahmyr Gibbs. The 26-year-old had a career year in 2025, recording 176 tackles, nine tackles for loss, five sacks, three forced fumbles and four passes defended. He was named a First Team All-Pro and earned his first Pro Bowl bid.

title: Lamar Jackson headed for injured reserve: Ravens QB to undergo surgery after injuring thumb vs. Bills - CBS Sports
description: Jackson made his first start on Sunday after missing the last three games
body:
Jackson made his first start on Sunday after missing the last three games

        The Baltimore Ravens probably feel like they're living in a nightmare right now. In Lamar Jackson's return to the field on Sunday, the two-time NFL MVP got knocked out of the game after suffering a thumb injury on Baltimore's first offensive play against the Buffalo Bills. Following the Ravens' 36-10 loss, the news went from bad to worse with head coach Jesse Minter revealing that Jackson would be placed on injured reserve. "That will be a surgery deal," Minter said. "He'll go to IR."Putting Jackson on IR means he'll miss at least four games. Here's a look at Baltimore's upcoming schedule: Week 9: Jaguars (Thursday night)Week 10: ChargersWeek 11: at PanthersWeek 12: at TexansWeek 13: Bye Week 14: Buccaneers
With Jackson now on injured reserve, the earliest he can return is for that Week 14 game against the Bucs on Dec. 13. Jackson has already missed three games this season due to injury, and this will bring his total to at least seven. The thumb injury happened on Baltimore's first offensive play of the game. On a first-and-10 play, Jackson threw a pass to Zay Flowers, but as he threw the ball, his hand hit a defender's arm, and after that happened, Jackson was in immediate pain. 
Jackson clearly didn't feel right, because he quickly ran to the sideline, and at that point, the Ravens' training staff took him into Baltimore's locker room at Highmark Stadium. 
The showdown between Jackson and Josh Allen was supposed to be one of the highlights in Week 8, but instead, it turned into a blowout win for Buffalo after Jackson left the game. The Ravens have already played three games without Jackson this year, and if those were any indication, things could get ugly over the next few weeks. With Jackson on the field during their first four games, the Ravens averaged 29.8 points per game while going 3-1. However, with Jackson out over the past three weeks, they went just 1-2 while averaging just 17.7 points per game. And now, you can add another loss to that tally in a game where the Ravens managed to score just 10 points. 
For Thursday's game against Jacksonville, it's still not clear who the starting QB will be. Not only did Jackson get hurt, but Tyler Huntley also had to leave the game after injuring his toe. If Huntley isn't ready to return, that means QB Joe Fagnano will be getting the first start of his career. Fagnano, an undrafted rookie out of UConn, went 10-of-12 for 91 yards with an interception while playing about 2.5 quarters against the Bills.
        
            
                Who is Ravens' Joe Fagnano? Baltimore turns to third QB after Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries
                
                    Zachary Pereles                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
For Jackson, there's no guarantee that he'll return as soon as he's eligible to come off IR. A thumb injury on the right hand is a brutal one for a quarterback because it impacts their ability to grip the football. Jackson will need that to fully heal before he can return, and since he has to undergo surgery, he likely won't be back on the field until late December. 
At 4-4, the Ravens will need to keep their head above water until then, or it could be a lost season for Baltimore.

Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield didn't complete any of his three throws in a 16-0 win

        The Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5) pulled off a 16-0, rain-soaked home victory against the Atlanta Falcons (3-5) on Sunday with a method not seen since 1945. With quarterback Baker Mayfield not completing any of his three passes, the Buccaneers are now the first team with no completions in a game since the 1974 Buffalo Bills, who won their completion-less game 16-12 against the New York Jets. Tampa Bay is also the first team since the 1945 Pittsburgh Steelers to win a game by double digits without having a completion. Those Steelers beat the Cardinals 23-0 in that game. Finally, the Buccaneers became the first team to produce no completions and over 300 yards rushing (324) in a game since the Boston Braves, now the Washington Commanders, in 1933. Mayfield returned from a three-game absence because of a right thumb dislocation in Tampa Bay's 43-13 road win at the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and with the heavy rain in Tampa on Sunday, the Buccaneers chose to lean exclusively on their ground game. They racked up 324 yards rushing, with running back Bucky Irving leading the way with 170 yards rushing and a touchdown on 27 carries. He also averaged 6.3 yards per carry. No. 2 running back Kenneth Gainwell also chipped in another 140 yards rushing on 25 carries for a 5.6 yards-per-carry average. Mayfield added 14 yards on the ground on four carries. Irving and Gainwell are now the first teammate duo in NFL history to each have 25-plus carries and 125-plus rushing yards in the same game. 
Incredibly, the Buccaneers have now won consecutive games against their NFC South division rivals, with Mayfield completing seven of his 14 throws for 64 yards and a touchdown in the last two weeks. They have survived a malfunctioning passing game because of their run game and smothering defense. In Week 7, they forced four Panthers turnovers, including a 32-yard fumble return touchdown. On Sunday against the Falcons, they forced Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. into a career-high four interceptions, and he completed just eight of his 24 throws for 125 yards. This is the first time a Falcons quarterback has thrown four interceptions in a game since Penix Jr.'s predecessor, Kirk Cousins, in a 17-13 Week 13 loss against the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2024 season. 
The Panthers stayed in first place in the NFC South with a 3-4 record entering Week 9, with the Buccaneers (3-5) and the Falcons (3-5) right behind them. The New Orleans Saints sit in last place at 2-5 and are on a bye in Week 8. Through the first half of the season, the NFC South remains the most wide-open, wacky division in the NFL.

description: Norvell was 41-39 in seven seasons and fell to 3-5 in 2026 after Saturday's loss to Clemson
body:
Norvell was 41-39 in seven seasons and fell to 3-5 in 2026 after Saturday's loss to Clemson
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026

    3:39 pm ET

            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After months of speculation about Mike Norvell's job security, Florida State decided to make a change and fired Norvell in his seventh season as coach of the Seminoles, the university announced on Sunday. For weeks, the sense from those in and around Florida State was that Norvell might be safe due to his enormous $46 million buyout and an athletic department in flux. However, those factors couldn't save Norvell. "We have made the decision to change the leadership of our football program," FSU president Richard McCullough said in a statement. "We thank Mike Norvell for his commitment and service to Florida State and wish him and his family the very best. We understand the deep passion of Seminole fans and share their high expectations for this program. We are confident in Rick Stockstill's ability to provide steady leadership during this transition. We will conduct a thorough national search for the program's next leader, someone who embraces Florida State's tradition of championship athletics and our standard of excellence." 
        
            
                Mike Norvell buyout: What it cost Florida State to move on from football coach 8 games into 7th season
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Apparently, the final straw for the power brokers at Florida State was Saturday's 36-24 loss to Clemson at home. The Seminoles weren't competitive for much of the game, and the Doak Campbell Stadium crowd dwindled  in the second half. 
The optics of a "Fire Mike Norvell" banner flying over the stadium prior to kickoff certainly didn't help, even if Dabo Swinney came to Norvell's defense. Along with Norvell, Florida State also fired defensive coordinator Tony White, whose unit has surrendered 31.6 points per game.Former Florida State quarterback and current director of scouting Rick Stockstill will take over as interim coach. Stockstill spent 18 seasons at MTSU and led the Blue Raiders to an overall record of 113-11 with 10 bowl appearances.
Norvell's tenure filled with ups and downsFlorida State hired Norvell in 2020, and he made noticeable progress in each of his first four seasons on the job. That culminated in a 13-1 season in 2023 in which the Seminoles won the ACC Championship but were left out of the four-team College Football Playoff after quarterback Jordan Travis went down with a late season-ending injury. That year, Norvell won Bobby Dodd Coach of the Year and ACC Coach of the Year. Since then, it's been a steady spiral downward for Norvell and the program as a whole. The 2024 season began with high expectations, but big whiffs in the transfer portal resulted in a disastrous 2-10 campaign. Over the last two seasons, Florida State has been well behind the curve on the NIL market, and it's struggled to compete at a high level. Since the start of that miserable 2024 season, Norvell has led the Seminoles to a10-22 record with no tangible signs of progress. 
Perhaps a coaching change will prompt a bigger investment into NIL and help Florida State close the gap with some of the biggest spenders in the ACC and college football at large. Norvell exits Tallahassee with an overall record of 41-39, and based on his track record prior to the 2024 season, he will get opportunities elsewhere. Prior to his Florida State tenure, Norvell had a successful four-season run at Memphis in which he compiled a 38-16 record and an American Athletic Conference championship. Norvell never recovered from 2024 Despite the frustrating way in which the 2023 season ended, optimism was high in Tallahassee coming into the 2024 campaign. The Seminoles pulled in a highly-touted transfer class that ranked seventh in the country, according to the 247Sports Team Rankings. 
In addition to landing D.J. Uiagalelei, Norvell and his staff poached a handful of talented players from Alabama. Among them were receiver Malik Benson, defensive back Earl Little Jr. and offensive lineman TJ Ferguson. Despite those additions, the Noles cratered on both sides of the ball. They scored just 15.4 points per game while allowing 28.0 points per game. The result was a disastrous 2-10 season from which Norvell never recovered. After that point, the Seminoles fell behind their peers on the NIL market, both in terms of funding and evaluation. Although Florida State landed the No. 8 transfer class in 2025, it resulted in just five wins. This past offseason, the Seminoles tumbled to No. 28 in the transfer class rankings, and it especially misread the market at quarterback. 
Florida State brought in Ashton Daniels, who has struggled mightily, and the Noles are set to miss a bowl for the third consecutive season. That 2024 failure started a backslide that Norvell and his staff could never stop.  What will FSU's future look like? The firing of Norvell ends months of speculation about his job security, but there are still more questions than answers about Florida State at the moment. 
First of all, what will happen atop the athletic department? The school is still looking for a full-time athletic director after firing Michael Alford in September. According to CBS Sports' own Richard Johnson, Florida State wants to embrace the new era of college athletics and find an athletic director who can find creative ways to create revenue for the department. Better late than never. The second question is about the candidate list Florida State will compile. Will the Seminoles want to go the route of up-and-coming Group of Six coach, which is what led them to Norvell during the last coaching search. That path can certainly work. Just look at the last two coaches hired out of James Madison. However, will the power brokers prefer a coach with a track record of winning at the Power Four level? Poaching a sitting coach will be more expensive, and it's fair to wonder whether the school will be able to rally the financial support to make that happen. If it can, a steady hand could provide the type of stability this program has needed for the last few years.

title: Ranking the 10 best women's college basketball players for 2026-27: Can anyone catch Sarah Strong? - CBS Sports
description: With JuJu Watkins back and Hannah Hidalgo off to a strong start, the POTY race is already a thriller
body:
With JuJu Watkins back and Hannah Hidalgo off to a strong start, the POTY race is already a thriller
        
        
                                                                                                            
                                                    By
                                                
                                                            CBS Sports Staff
                                                    
                    
                                    
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:56 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        There was a full 14 hours between the end of the WNBA season in Game 7 on Saturday, Oct. 31, in San Francisco and the tip-off of the women's college basketball season in Rome, Italy, on Nov. 1. Hope you enjoyed your offseason, women's hoops fans. The 2026-27 college season got off to a high-scoring start, with Notre Dame beating Villanova 99-75 at the Eternal City Tip-Off behind Hannah Hidalgo's 32 points, seven rebounds, eight assists and three assists. Most other top players will start their seasons on Monday, including JuJu Watkins, who returns to the USC lineup after missing all of last season recovering from an ACL tear. Watkins will make her debut against UNLV at 4 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network and streaming on Paramount+.
        
            
                Women's college basketball rankings: JuJu Watkins has USC at No. 3 in AP Top 25, South Carolina begins on top
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
There are many talented players in Division I, but we compiled a list of the top players to keep an eye on. Without giving away spoilers, here are CBS Sports' top 10 women's college basketball players ahead of the 2026-27 season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Toby FournierDespite a shaky start last season while facing some tough opponents, Duke turned things around and won both the ACC regular season and conference tournament titles before making it to the Elite Eight. Fournier was the key component to this success as the team's leader in scoring, rebounding and blocks. After not starting any games as a freshman and still winning ACC rookie of the year, the 6-foot-2 forward thrived as a starter last season with 17.3 points on 52.5% shooting from the field, 7.9 rebounds and 2.2 blocks per game. 
Fournier demonstrates her power and athleticism with her ability to finish at the rim. In fact, her two-handed dunk has become a signature move for her during pre-game warmups. However, she also has great footwork and her high motor makes her dangerous in transition. Her 6-foot-5 wingspan and basketball IQ also make her a threat on defense.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Olivia OlsonThe Wolverines are fresh off a historic 28–7 overall season and a trip to the Elite Eight with Olson as their leading scorer and rebounder. The 6-foot-1 guard averaged 18.9 points per game as a sophomore while shooting 46.8% as a crafty and versatile scorer. Her body control, even mid-air, allows her to finish even if she gets bumped by a defender. She is also not afraid to crash the boards, which is clear from her 6.1 boards per contest.One of her most memorable games last season was her career-high 31 points in an 88-86 overtime win against Ohio State on Feb. 25. That performance also included nine rebounds, four assists and, most notably, the game-winner with 3.2 remaining in the extra period.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Audi CrooksCrooks was the top player in the transfer portal this offseason and, now she will be playing her senior year at Oklahoma State. The 6-foot-3 center was averaging more than one point per minute in the first part of last season and she currently holds the longest active Division I women's college basketball streak for consecutive games scoring in double figures. Crooks' only college boxscore with fewer than 10 points was during her very first game as a freshman in 2023. Her size and physical strength, combined with elite footwork, make her a force to be reckoned with in the paint. She wrapped up the 2025-26 campaign as the nation's second leading scorer with 25.8 points per contest while shooting 64.9% from the field. This includes her career-high 47 points while shooting 19 of 25 from the field in a 106-95 win over Indiana on Nov. 30.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Jaloni CambridgeCambridge's sophomore season ended in a loss to Notre Dame in the second round of the NCAA Tournament, but she put on an admirable fight in the defeat with 41 points on 52% shooting from the field while going 5 of 8 from beyond the arc. She is coming off a breakout season and it will be fun to see if she can bring that momentum into her junior year. 
Cambridge scored in double figures in every single game last season, including 21 outings with 20+ points. She averaged 23.2 points per game on 49.4% shooting, which made her the Big Ten's leading scorer and No. 6 in the nation. The 5-foot-7 point guard is quick, efficient and shows up to the court every day with a "whatever it takes" attitude instilled by her dad. Besides her scoring, she also contributed 5.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.9 steals per game.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Joyce EdwardsEdwards is a versatile weapon for South Carolina who impacts the game on both sides of the court. Her speed and high basketball IQ help her turn defense into offense with a strong transition game. She confidently attacks the rim and is able to finish through contact.The 6-foot-3 forward finished her sophomore year averaging a team-high 19.2 points per game while shooting 57.1% from the field. In the process, she set a new South Carolina single-season scoring record with a total of 768 points. Edwards also led the Gamecocks with 1.8 steals per game, along with 1.1 blocks per contest. Coach Dawn Staley has praised her ball-handling skills and even compared her to former Gamecock and current WNBA superstar A'ja Wilson.
"I think Joyce probably can handle the ball a little bit better than A'ja when A'ja was her age," Staley said. "Joyce probably gets a lot of harder scores than A'ja just by mere height. A'ja's got a little bit more height on her."

                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Madison BookerLet's get this out of the way: Booker had the worst game of her career during the Final Four matchup against UCLA, but that performance by no means defines her as a player. Booker averaged 18.9 points per game while shooting 50.8% from the floor last season. She set a new career high of 40 points while shooting 66.7% in a 100-58 win over Oregon in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. Booker models her game after NBA star Kevin Durant, which clearly reflects through her elite mid-range skills and footwork. She is an athletic forward with a high basketball IQ and the ability to step in as point guard -- which we saw during her freshman year when Rori Harmon was injured. On the other side of the court, Booker uses her physical advantage and quick hands to be disruptive on defense, which is a non-negotiable for anyone who plays for Vic Schaefer. With Harmon now in the WNBA, this will be an exciting year for Booker as she steps into a veteran leadership role.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Mikayla BlakesBlakes is one of the most exciting high-volume scorers in college basketball and has been in the spotlight since her freshman season, which featured two 50+ point games. Her 55 points against Auburn in February 2025 broke Elena Delle Donne's Division I freshman single-game scoring record. As a sophomore last season, Blakes led the nation in scoring with 27.1 points per game, including 12 games in which she scored 30+ points. Her 918 total points set a new NCAA Division I sophomore single-season scoring record. What makes this even more impressive is that Blakes doesn't have to rely on 3-point shooting. She shoots 45.6% from the field but just 35.9% from beyond the arc -- although she is dangerous from anywhere when she gets hot. Her basketball IQ and ability to control her speed help her get past defenders. Meanwhile, she can also make an impact on defense as she averaged 2.9 steals per game, which put her in the top 25 in the nation. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. JuJu WatkinsBy the time USC plays its season opener, it will have been about 19 months since Watkins tore her ACL during the second round of the 2025 NCAA Tournament. However, her comeback is one of the biggest storylines this season. Watkins is a modern wing whose skills allow her to play shooting guard or point guard. She is a three-level scorer, a strong playmaker and a versatile defender. Most notably, she helped the Trojans reach a level of success they hadn't seen since the '90s. 
Watkins set the NCAA Division I women's basketball freshman scoring record with 920 points during the 2023-24 season. In the process, she led the Trojans to their first Elite Eight appearance since 1994. The following year, she earned the 2024-25 Naismith Player of the Year award while averaging 23.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 2.2 steals and 1.8 blocks per game. It was hard to figure out where to rank Watkins since she's been out for so long, but her level of talent and what she showed before her injury makes her a player who should not be underestimated. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Hannah HidalgoThe energy Hidalgo plays with every time she steps on the court is the definition of a "dawg." She might be an undersized guard, but you can't ever count her out. Hidalgo led the Fighting Irish all the way to the Elite Eight despite a major roster turnover last season. She dominated in the Sweet Sixteen victory against Vanderbilt with 31 points, 11 rebounds, 10 steals, seven assists and a block. She was just as impressive during the regular season, averaging 25.3 points, 6.9 rebounds, 5.2 assists, 5.6 steals per game. Hidalgo's efforts on offense made her the nation's third-leading scorer. Meanwhile, she also set a new Division I single season steals record -- an effort that earned her the Naismith Defensive Player of the Year award. As she begins her senior year, Hidalgo will be the only returning player for Notre Dame. A major rebuild like that usually leaves a lot of questions for a team, but with Hidalgo on the roster, the Fighting Irish are certainly in good hands.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Sarah StrongThe UConn star was named the 2026 Naismith Player of the Year because of her efficiency and how complete her game is. Throughout her sophomore season, Strong averaged 18.4 points per game as a three-level scorer. She shot 58.2% from the field and over 40% from 3-point range, while also registering 7.7 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 3.4 steals and 1.6 blocks per contest.To make those numbers even more impressive, coach Geno Auriemma revealed that Strong had not been 100% all season because she tweaked her Achilles tendon while playing 3x3 basketball for USA Basketball in Mongolia during the summer of 2025. Strong will likely be even more dangerous this upcoming season as she spent the summer resting. The talent is there, but this year will be all about growing as a leader and getting comfortable with the spotlight now that Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd – who she considers her mentors- are no longer around.

title: Mike Norvell fired: Buyout, contract details as Florida State ousts coach in 7th season - CBS Sports
description: The Seminoles are looking at a hefty payout for Norvell after moving on from their seventh-year coach
body:
The Seminoles are looking at a hefty payout for Norvell after moving on from their seventh-year coach
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:19 pm ET

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Florida State fired seventh-year coach Mike Norvell on Sunday, parting ways following the Seminoles' 36-24 home loss to Clemson on Saturday that featured countless empty seats during a multi-possession game in the fourth quarter.The team's third consecutive ACC loss was the 17th setback for Norvell in his last 21 games against league competition, a horrid stretch that kept him on the hot seat each of the last two years.Norvell's buyout is estimated just under $49 million — roughly 85% of his remaining salary through a contract running through the 2031 season — which would be the third-biggest payout in college football history. That figure is behind only the $77 million paid to Jimbo Fisher at Texas A&M and LSU's $54 million check to Brian Kelly last cycle. Norvell's remaining deal is subject to mitigation and could be offset and reduced if he lands another coaching job.
Norvell signed a lucrative contract extension following the 2023 season, when the Seminoles went undefeated in the regular season and won the ACC title -- only to be snubbed from the College Football Playoff due to quarterback injuries. With Nick Saban retiring at Alabama that same cycle, Norvell found just the right leverage to get a massive extension from Florida State that thrust him onto the list of the top 10 highest-paid coaches in the country. That contract has aged like milk as the Seminoles went 7-17 over the 2024 and 2025 seasons, which made 2026 a make-or-break year in Tallahassee for Norvell. Norvell's contract, buyout detailsNorvell's extension after the 2023 season may go down as one of the most regrettable deals a program has made in recent memory, as it tacked on two extra years through 2031 and raised his salary by more than $2 million per year. That made it prohibitively expensive for Florida State to move on from Norvell, and the calculus in Tallahassee coming into the 2026 campaign was measuring whether it's worth waiting for the buyout to drop or risk finding out there's still further to dig before hitting rock bottom.
Norvell is set to earn $10.3 million in salary for the 2026 season, and has five years and $54.75 million remaining on his contract after this year. After his in-season firing on Sunday, the Seminoles owe Norvell just over $48.6 million -- 85% of the remaining five years plus $3 million and an additional $750,000 as part of a recently-renegotiated buyout agreement. That would be just below the amount Penn State was scheduled to pay James Franklin when they fired him last year, but Franklin and Penn State agreed to reduce the $49 million buyout to just $9 million as he was set to become Virginia Tech's new coach. 
Norvell may not have the same immediate opportunities as Franklin, and the Seminoles can't bank on such a drastic reduction in cost. As such, it's a considerable financial commitment from Florida State's boosters to move on from Norvell, but one they were willing to pay to cut ties entering November.

title: Andy Reid backs decision to trust Harrison Butker despite Chiefs kicker's struggles - CBS Sports
description: Butker's late miss helped give Denver an opportunity to complete its comeback and intensified questions about Kan
body:
Butker's late miss helped give Denver an opportunity to complete its comeback and intensified questions about Kansas City's kicker situation
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:19 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Kansas City Chiefs have a kicker problem. Harrison Butker missed yet another kick on Sunday, a 54-yarder that would have extended Kansas City's lead over the division rival Denver Broncos to six points but instead set up the game-winning touchdown drive by Denver.The Chiefs led by three points when they drove down to the Denver 30-yard line and faced third-and-2 from there. Patrick Mahomes dropped back to pass, but he was sacked for a six-yard loss, which turned what would have been a 48-yard field goal attempt into a 54-yarder, and Butker missed his kick wide to the right.
It was the third significant miss in two weeks for Butker, whose job already appeared to be on thin ice after the Chiefs signed former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad earlier this week. Tucker had been out of the league since 2024 after he was accused by multiple women of sexual misconduct, as originally reported by The Baltimore Banner. After the game, Andy Reid defended the decision to send Butker out to try the deep field goal attempt."Those are hindsight. It ended up being what it was," Reid said, via FOX 4 Kansas City. "But it's within Harrison's range."
Here's the thing, though: 54 yards isn't really within Butker's range anymore. It may have been during his prime, but these days, he is not nearly consistent enough from that distance to justify trying that kick.Here's what we wrote just last week, for example, when Butker missed a pair of field goal attempts in the Chiefs' loss to the Seattle Seahawks:
Through 2023, he made 89.1% of his total field goals, and 28 of 40 (70%) from beyond 50 yards. Since then, though, Butker has made just 82.2% of his kicks, and only 8-of-18 (44.4%) from beyond 50 yards. He missed one of those 50-plus-yard kicks short by several yards in this game, making him just 1-of-5 from 50-plus this year, and he missed another from 45 yards out, pushing it wide to the right. Whether you agree with the decision to kick the field goal or not, it's clear that the Chiefs can't trust Butker in big spots anymore. And that means his time with the Chiefs could soon be coming to an end, whether Kansas City turns to Tucker or somebody else.
